description: We are a four-member team from AI & ML and Data Science, passionate about artificial intelligence, Earth observation, and space technology. Our team combines AI/ML development, programming, data science, and analytical skills to build innovative solutions using NASA-ISRO NISAR data. We welcome teammates with expertise in SAR remote sensing, GIS, geospatial analysis, and scientific research to join our mission!
summary:
TerraTrace AI is an AI-powered geospatial intelligence platform developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the challenge "Dancing with the SARs." It uses real NASA-ISRO NISAR L-band Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) observations to identify and investigate changes in Earth's surface over time.

Using Bengaluru, Karnataka, as our initial study area, TerraTrace AI analyses two NISAR observations acquired on October 29 and November 10, 2026. It processes HH and HV polarization measurements, compares temporal radar backscatter, identifies candidate surface-change regions, and visualizes the results through interactive maps, geospatial overlays, and statistical analysis.

Powered by a LangGraph-based AI agent, the platform connects specialized analysis tools and generates evidence-grounded explanations while preserving scientific uncertainty and data provenance.

Our vision is to make complex satellite radar observations accessible for monitoring urban landscapes, vegetation, water bodies, and other environmental changes, helping researchers and communities make better-informed decisions for a changing planet.
details:
TerraTrace AI: NISAR-Powered Earth Surface Change Intelligence

1. Project Overview

TerraTrace AI is an AI-powered geospatial intelligence platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 under the challenge "Dancing with the SARs." The platform leverages NASA-ISRO NISAR (NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar) observations to analyse, identify, and visualize changes occurring on Earth's surface over time.

The project focuses on transforming complex satellite radar measurements into accessible geospatial information through temporal analysis, automated change detection, interactive visualization, and agentic AI orchestration.

2. System Architecture and Methodology

TerraTrace AI follows a modular processing architecture consisting of several interconnected components.

NISAR Data Acquisition and Validation: The platform works with real NISAR L-band Level-2 GCOV observations. It validates product metadata, acquisition dates, polarization availability, spatial coverage, coordinate reference systems, and data integrity before processing.

SAR Data Processing: HDF5-based NISAR products are inspected to extract available HH and HV polarization measurements. The processing pipeline performs data-quality checks, backscatter preparation, geospatial extraction, and spatial alignment to support temporal comparison.

Temporal Backscatter Analysis: Radar backscatter measurements from different acquisition dates are compared to identify variations in surface response. The system generates polarization-specific difference layers and statistical summaries.

Change Detection and Geospatial Analysis: Statistical screening techniques identify candidate radar-change regions. The resulting outputs include change masks, GeoJSON polygons, spatial statistics, and estimated candidate-change areas.

Agentic AI Orchestration: A LangGraph-based agent coordinates specialized analysis tools through task classification, tool selection, execution tracking, and evidence integration. This enables structured analysis workflows and traceable processing.

Interactive Visualization: A React-based dashboard with Leaflet mapping capabilities presents satellite observations, HH/HV comparisons, temporal difference maps, candidate regions, and geospatial statistics.

Evidence-Based Reporting: The platform organizes processing metadata, analytical outputs, geospatial evidence, and scientific limitations into understandable results and reporting workflows.

3. Bengaluru Case Study

Bengaluru, Karnataka, serves as the initial study area for demonstrating the platform's capabilities. The implementation uses two real NISAR L-band GCOV observations acquired on 29 October 2026 and 10 November 2026.

The observations contain HH and HV polarization measurements, which are extracted and analysed on a common 10-metre geospatial grid using the EPSG:32643 coordinate reference system.

The temporal analysis has generated polarization-specific difference maps, candidate change masks, spatial regions, and statistical summaries. The current results identify 5,741 HH candidate pixels and 3,762 HV candidate pixels, corresponding to estimated candidate areas of 57.41 hectares and 37.62 hectares, respectively.

These results represent candidate radar-backscatter anomalies and require independent supporting evidence before being attributed to specific environmental or human activities.

4. Technology Stack

The platform integrates technologies across artificial intelligence, backend development, geospatial processing, and interactive visualization.

  • Programming Languages: Python and JavaScript.
  • Backend: FastAPI.
  • Frontend: React.js and Vite.
  • Agentic AI: LangGraph.
  • AI/ML: PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, BLIP, and PEFT.
  • Geospatial Processing: HDF5, h5py, Rasterio, GeoPandas, NumPy, and GDAL-compatible tools.
  • Visualization: Leaflet, Matplotlib, and interactive geospatial overlays.
  • Data Format: HDF5, GeoTIFF, and GeoJSON.
  • Primary Data Source: NASA-ISRO NISAR observations.

5. Innovation and Technical Contributions

TerraTrace AI integrates NISAR radar processing, temporal backscatter analysis, geospatial change detection, and agentic AI within a unified application.

Its modular architecture connects specialized analytical tools through an auditable agent workflow. Rather than presenting radar imagery as isolated visual outputs, the platform links observations, polarization measurements, temporal differences, candidate regions, and supporting metadata.

The combination of scientific processing and interactive geospatial visualization makes complex radar observations more understandable and accessible to users with different levels of remote-sensing expertise.

6. Benefits and Intended Impact

TerraTrace AI aims to support more accessible and informed monitoring of Earth's changing surface. Its potential applications include investigating urban surface changes, vegetation variations, water-body dynamics, and flood-related surface changes.

The platform is intended to benefit researchers, environmental analysts, urban planners, resource managers, and decision-makers by providing interactive spatial evidence and temporal comparisons.

By integrating NISAR observations with complementary optical, environmental, and geospatial datasets, the system can be extended to support broader environmental assessment and future disaster-monitoring applications.

7. Scientific Reliability and Responsible Interpretation

Data integrity, geospatial compatibility, reproducibility, and uncertainty are central considerations in the development of TerraTrace AI.

The platform preserves source observation metadata and distinguishes measured radar variations from algorithm-generated candidate changes and possible environmental interpretations. It does not treat backscatter anomalies as confirmed flooding, construction, deforestation, or urban expansion without independent corroboration.

This approach promotes transparent and scientifically responsible interpretation of satellite observations.

8. Future Development

Future development will focus on supporting additional NISAR observations, multiple study areas, longer temporal sequences, complementary Earth-observation datasets, and improved independent validation.

The long-term vision is to evolve TerraTrace AI into a scalable, agentic Earth-observation intelligence platform that transforms satellite radar data into accessible, evidence-grounded insights for understanding and monitoring a continuously changing planet.
